cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Browser caching lets the browser reuse responses it already downloaded, controlled by the server's Cache-Control and validator headers. A fresh response within max-age is used with no request at all.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: A stale response is revalidated with If-None-Match; the server answers 304 Not Modified with no body if unchanged. You cannot purge users' browsers, so give static assets content-hashed filenames with a one-year immutable TTL and serve HTML as no-cache. Prefer filenames over ?v= query strings.

questions.q: Why can't you purge a bad file from users' browsers?
questions.a: The cache lives on millions of devices you don't control. You can only change URLs or wait for expiry.

questions.q: What does immutable add to max-age?
questions.a: It tells the browser not to revalidate even on reload, saving 304 round trips.

questions.q: After a release, some users see a blank page. Why?
questions.a: Cached HTML references asset files the deploy removed, so JS returns 404. Make HTML no-cache and keep old assets a while.
